name: Okra (Bhindi)
perishability: Highly perishable. 2–3 days at room temperature before pods toughen and blacken.
summary: A warm-season vegetable that India grows more of than any other country. Pods are picked every two or three days and lose quality within a day, so supply tracks temperature: plentiful in summer and the monsoon, scarce and dear in the North Indian winter when the plant stops growing.

key_numbers.label: World rank
key_numbers.note: India grows well over half of world okra

key_numbers.label: Export
key_numbers.note: a leading fresh-vegetable export to the UK and Gulf

global: India is the largest okra producer and a major exporter of fresh okra by air to the UK, UAE and the Gulf, mainly from Gujarat and Maharashtra.

states.basis: Major producing states (ranked approximately; shares not shown)

belts.name: Bengal and Bihar plains
belts.note: Summer and monsoon supply to the East and Delhi.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.note: High quality; pest pressure rises with heat.

seasons.name: Kharif (rainy)
seasons.note: Yellow vein mosaic is worst in this season.

seasons.name: Winter (South and West)
seasons.note: Only mild-winter areas supply in winter.

lean_season: November–February in North India, when cold stops growth.

climate.v: 25–35 °C ideal. Seeds barely germinate below 20 °C; flowers drop above ~42 °C.
Killed by frost; growth stalls below ~15 °C.
Regular irrigation in summer; waterlogging rots roots in the monsoon.

weather_risks.impact: Growth stops; supply falls and prices climb.
Flower drop and tough, curved pods.

pests.name: Yellow vein mosaic virus
pests.impact: The main constraint; yellow-netted leaves and unmarketable pods.

postharvest.chilling: Chilling injury below ~7 °C: pitting and darkening.
practices: Picked tender (8–10 cm) in the early morning; over-mature pods are fibrous.
Packed loosely in ventilated bags or crates; bruising blackens pods.
Export okra is graded by length, packed in 5 kg cartons and air-freighted the same day.

steps.what: Same-day auction; prices change sharply day to day.
Vendors, quick commerce, and export pack houses near Ahmedabad and Mumbai airports.

supply_chain.packaging: Jute or leno bags, crates; 5 kg cartons for export.
supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

varieties.name: Arka Anamika, Arka Abhay
varieties.note: ICAR-IIHR; tolerant to yellow vein mosaic.

varieties.name: Kashi Kranti, Kashi Pragati, Kashi Lalima (red)

trade.exports: Fresh okra by air to the UK, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and other Gulf states; frozen okra too.

policy.what: Export consignments need residue testing and phytosanitary certificates (EU and UK rules).

history.what: North Indian winter shortage; retail often ₹80–120/kg.
Peak pickings push farm prices down to ₹5–10/kg.

signals: Night temperatures in North India in Nov–Feb.
Whitefly and mosaic reports in the kharif season.
business: Freshness is everything: same-day sourcing and gentle handling decide the grade.
Winter supply from Gujarat and the South to North India is the main arbitrage.
Export-grade okra (sorted, length-graded) commands premiums in Indian metros too.
